chung.Description:
Description:
- This course will arm students with the conceptual and technical knowledge needed to develop 2D game projects. There are a series of foundations for experimentation and exploration of video game design, story, character development, and winning gameplay before programming begins. The courses emphasize the self-reliance and personal expression of the gaming artist, and encourage you to take conceptual risks and develop new modes of expression and form through gaming. There will be also a series of tutorials to develop gameplay without coding.

Objective:
- Understand primary concepts of gaming, and an exploration of how these basic concepts affect the way gamers interact with our games.
- Understand what defines a “game” and the mechanics and rules behind different types of games.
- Examine how storytelling acts as a vital mechanism for driving video gameplay forward.
- Understand game story flows and the strategic elements of gameplay.
- Investigate key components of environment and level design.
- Create successful character designs that can be applied to video games
- Complete a 2d game project.
Teaching method:
Under lecturer’s instruction, through a series of instruction sessions, tutorials, work analysis and group exercises, students will be equipped with knowledge and skills to complete a game project.

clo: Describe the basic structure of a 2D game, identify the roles in the game development process, and outline the key principles and steps of 2D game art development.
Develop a Game Design Document (GDD) that includes story, world building, character and environment systems, gameplay structure, core mechanics, and both game flow and UI flow.
Create a complete 2D game art asset system including character design and animation, environment, items, UI and visual effects.
Build a functional mini-game using appropriate game engine and platforms.
Apply AI tools and demonstrate AI literacy to collaborate effectively.
Demonstrate professionalism in teamwork and workflow.
danhGia: Participation grade will be given based on students' attendance, students' attitude, preparation, contribution of discussions

Students will start from a brief provided by the instructor or propose their own 2D game idea for approval. Develop an original 2D game concept covering storyline and hook, worldbuilding, gameplay structure and core mechanics, game flow, UI flow, character system, environments, props, and item system.
AI tools may be applied responsibly for ideation and consistency checks, with prompts, outputs, and refinements documented.

The final submission is a detailed Game Design Document (GDD) that clearly defines and describes the planned game, presented in a professional format with full citations of sources and AI use.

Understand and apply the process of developing a comprehensive 2D Game Design Document.
Demonstrate the ability to integrate storyline, worldbuilding, gameplay mechanics, game flow, UI flow, and asset systems into a cohesive concept.
Practice creativity and originality in concept development.

Group assignment of 3–4 students, carried out in class and at home over 2 weeks.
Teams will present progress in stages, get feedback from the instructor, and update their work accordingly.
During review sessions, students must present how AI was used, discuss AI-generated issues with the instructor, and justify their design choices before the final presentation.
Students must document updates and manage different report versions as part of the submission.
Based on the studied LO, lecturer will instruct students how to ideal, research & develop their specific game project

Based on the approved Game Design Document, create a complete 2D asset package ready for development. The package must include characters, animations, environments, props, items, UI elements, and visual effects, each with a research board, references, and design rationale. All assets must align with the narrative and worldbuilding, support gameplay actions, and maintain aesthetic strength, distinct style, and visual coherence, with brief explorations and a justified final selection.

The final submission is a bundled asset package containing all required visual components presented in a structured format, ready for integration into the game engine.

Apply principles of visual design and consistency to produce cohesive 2D game assets, maintain alignment with narrative, worldbuilding, and gameplay mechanics.

Present a professional game art package prepared for implementation in the development phase.

Group assignment of 3–4 students, carried out in class and at home over 2 weeks.
Teams will present progress in stages, get feedback from the instructor, and update their work accordingly.
During review sessions, students must present how AI was used, discuss AI-generated issues with the instructor, and justify their design choices before the final presentation.
Students must document updates and manage different report versions as part of the submission.
Based on the studied LO, lecturer will instruct students how to develop the conceptual art for the game project.

Students will build a runnable 2D game in Unity using assets from Assignment 2 and the approved GDD, integrating complete game flow and UI flow, and ensuring a fully playable level from start to finish. Code may be provided, downloaded, or self-written or modified, and the project must also include professional advertising and showcase materials to present the game proposal effectively.
The final submission is playable build, advertising or showcase content.

Learn to integrate 2D assets into Unity, manage animation, VFX, UI, and scene flow, and apply or adapt code at a functional level to connect visuals with gameplay.
Gain experience in presenting and promoting their project professionally through advertising and showcase outputs.

Group assignment of 3–4 students, carried out in class and at home over 2 weeks.
Teams will present progress in stages, get feedback from the instructor, and update their work accordingly.
During review sessions, students must present how AI was used, discuss AI-generated issues with the instructor, and justify their design choices before the final presentation.
Students must document updates and manage different report versions as part of the submission.
Based on the studied LO, lecturer will instruct students how to complete their game project.
